sillosuchus:research:1.title: 2026 in archosaur paleontology (research: General pseudosuchian research)

facts.statement: Sillosuchus lived in South America during the Late Triassic period.
facts.quote: Sillosuchus is a genus of large (femur length = 47 cm in the holotype) shuvosaurid poposauroid archosaur that lived in South America during the Late Triassic period.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen of Sillosuchus was discovered in the Ischigualasto Formation in northwestern Argentina.
facts.quote: The holotype specimen of Sillosuchus, PVSJ 85, is a partial skeleton discovered in sediments of the Ischigualasto Formation, Cancha de Bochas Member in the Ischigualasto-Villa Unión Basin in northwestern Argentina.

facts.statement: Additional remains were first described by Dr. William Sill in 1974 but were initially attributed to the genus Saurosuchus.
facts.quote: Possible additional remains were first described by Dr. William Sill in 1974, though he referred them to Saurosuchus, a giant quadrupedal predator distantly related to Sillosuchus.

facts.statement: A specimen (PVL 2472) contains a large isolated cervical vertebra measuring 20 cm in length.
facts.quote: One specimen, PVL 2472, includes fragments of the tibia, ankle, and a large isolated cervical (neck vertebra), 20 cm long.

facts.statement: In 2011, Nesbitt re-evaluated large fragments previously assigned to Sillosuchus and found they shared distinctive features with the holotype but were much larger.
facts.quote: Nesbitt (2011) briefly reconsidered these large fragments, and found that they showed several distinctive features akin to the Sillosuchus holotype, mostly differing in their much larger size.

facts.statement: The specific name longicervix refers to the genus's elongated cervical vertebrae.
facts.quote: The specific name, longicervix, refers to the elongated cervical vertebrae of the genus.

facts.statement: Sillosuchus is the only named bipedal poposauroid known from outside North America.
facts.quote: Sillosuchus is the only named genus of bipedal poposauroid currently known from outside North America.

facts.statement: The genus was described in 1997 by paleontologists Oscar Alcober and J. Michael Parrish.
facts.quote: El género fue descrito en 1997 por los paleontólogos Oscar Alcober y J. Michael Parrish.

facts.statement: Fossil remains of Sillosuchus were discovered in the Ischigualasto Formation in the province of San Juan, Argentina.
facts.quote: Los restos fósiles de Sillosuchus fueron descubiertos en sedimentos de la Formación Ischigualasto, en la provincia de San Juan, Argentina.

facts.statement: Shuvosaurids were bipedal, lightly armored reptiles with dinosaur-like hip and skull structures, despite being closely related to modern crocodilians.
facts.quote: Shuvosaurids were an unusual family of reptiles belonging to the group Poposauroidea; although their closest modern relatives are crocodilians, they were bipedal and lightly armored, with dinosaur-like hip and skull structures.

facts.statement: Based on related species, shuvosaurids like Sillosuchus were likely toothless, beaked herbivores.
facts.quote: Based on skull remains from members of the family such as Effigia, they were also toothless and likely beaked herbivores.

facts.statement: Sillosuchus had large excavations or pockets on the sides of its neck and back vertebrae, a trait used to distinguish it from Saurosuchus.
facts.quote: Sillosuchus had several unique features compared to its relatives. The neck and back vertebrae had large excavations or pockets on the side, an unusual trait that assisted paleontologists in assigning the giant cervical vertebra to Sillosuchus rather than Saurosuchus.

facts.statement: Sillosuchus had short, fused ischia that were flattened top-to-bottom, unlike the side-to-side flattening seen in most other reptiles.
facts.quote: The left and right ischia (rear-pointing hip bones) were short and fused to each other. They were also flattened in a dorsoventral (top-to-bottom) direction, unlike the case in most other reptiles in which they were flattened in a mediolateral (side-to-side) direction.

facts.statement: Sillosuchus was a large archosaur characterized by its long and slender neck.
facts.quote: Sillosuchus era un arcosaurio de gran tamaño caracterizado por su cuello largo y esbelto.

facts.statement: The cervical vertebrae of Sillosuchus had deep cavities called pleuroceli, possibly related to pneumatic structures in the axial skeleton.
facts.quote: Las vértebras cervicales presentaban cavidades profundas denominadas pleurocelos, que podrían estar relacionadas con la presencia de estructuras neumáticas en el esqueleto axial.

facts.statement: Comparative studies suggest Sillosuchus likely had a light body and a bipedal posture, despite the lack of complete skull remains.
facts.quote: Aunque no se han encontrado restos craneales completos, estudios comparativos con otros poposáuridos indican que probablemente poseía un cuerpo ligero y una postura bípeda.

facts.statement: Sillosuchus lived in a warm, seasonal environment with river-crossed alluvial plains and abundant vegetation.
facts.quote: Durante el período en el que vivió Sillosuchus, la región presentaba un ambiente cálido y estacional, con llanuras aluviales atravesadas por ríos y áreas de vegetación abundante.

facts.statement: Sillosuchus belongs to the family Shuvosauridae within the group Poposauroidea.
facts.quote: Shuvosaurids were an unusual family of reptiles belonging to the group Poposauroidea; although their closest modern relatives are crocodilians, they were bipedal and lightly armored, with dinosaur-like hip and skull structures.

facts.statement: Sillosuchus is classified as a member of Poposauridae, a group of archosaurs in the clade Pseudosuchia more closely related to crocodilians than to dinosaurs.
facts.quote: Sillosuchus fue clasificado como miembro de Poposauridae, un grupo de arcosaurios del clado Pseudosuchia relacionado más estrechamente con los cocodrilos que con los dinosaurios.

facts.statement: A 2011 analysis by Sterling Nesbitt confirmed Sillosuchus's position within Poposauroidea.
facts.quote: El análisis realizado por Sterling Nesbitt en 2011 redefinió las relaciones evolutivas de numerosos arcosaurios triásicos y confirmó la posición de Sillosuchus dentro de Poposauroidea.

facts.statement: A fossil reconstruction was presented in 2008 by the National University of San Juan as a tribute to Dr. William Dudley Sill.
facts.quote: A reconstruction of the fossil was presented in 2008 by the National University of San Juan in Argentina, in an homage to Dr. William Dudley Sill who was an important promoter of paleontology in San Juan.

facts.statement: It is debated whether the long neck of Sillosuchus was a unique trait or simply typical for shuvosaurids.
facts.quote: Later studies have shown that, while the neck of Sillosuchus was long compared to most pseudosuchians, this trait was par for the course for shuvosaurids.

facts.statement: The genus Sillosuchus was named by Alcober and Parrish in 1997.
facts.quote: PBDB name: Sillosuchus (genus), Alcober and Parrish 1997

facts.statement: Sillosuchus belongs to the family Shuvosauridae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Shuvosauridae

facts.statement: Sillosuchus is classified as a reptile.
facts.quote: Class: Reptilia

facts.statement: Sillosuchus lived during the Carnian stage, between 237 and 227.3 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Carnian to Carnian (237 to 227.3 million years ago)

facts.statement: The type species of the genus Sillosuchus is Sillosuchus longicervix.
facts.quote: Type species: Sillosuchus longicervix

facts.statement: Only one fossil occurrence of Sillosuchus has been recorded in the database.
facts.quote: Fossil occurrences recorded: 1

facts.statement: A 2026 study by Ponce, Cerda, and Desojo analyzed the histology of limb bones in Sillosuchus longicervix to investigate diverse growth rates among pseudosuchians.
facts.quote: Evidence from the study of the histology of appendicular elements of Saurosuchus galilei, Sillosuchus longicervix, Aetobarbakinoides brasiliensis, Aetosauroides scagliai, Gracilisuchus stipanicicorum, Tarjadia ruthae and Riojasuchus tenuisceps, indicative of diversity of growth rates of the studied pseudosuchians, is presented by Ponce, Cerda & Desojo (2026).

rejected.statement: The genus name Sillosuchus honors Dr. William Sill and includes the Greek word 'suchus' meaning crocodile.
rejected.quote: The generic name of Sillosuchus refers to Dr. William Sill, and suchus, from the Greek word meaning 'crocodile'.
